Subject: Post-demo: procurement path & packaging options

Hi Jessica — thanks again for the demo time today. Quick recap + a couple of asks so procurement can start lining up internal steps:

Summary from our side:
- Pilot objective: validate integrated retrieval latency and 99th percentile response time at 500 QPS for customer-facing summarization.
- Suggested start: Hosted (on-demand) for a 4–6 week pilot to avoid procurement friction, then evaluate Dedicated reserved capacity if performance/cost signal justifies it.

Questions for procurement team (cc'd):
1) Preferred buying instrument: corporate card for pilot or PO/contract required up front?
2) Marketplace interest: do you prefer processing via AWS Marketplace (metered billing) vs direct PO to Redwood?
3) Timeline: target date when your procurement/legal needs an executed MSA/SOW to include Redwood as a vendor?

Attachments: BrightLeaf-post-demo-summary.pdf (short one-pager with the pilot plan)

If PO is required, we can provide a short-form commercial addendum + SOW template. If card is acceptable for the pilot, we can start immediately once you enable an API key and we exchange a minimal NAC (data processing note).

Next step proposal: can we lock a 30-minute procurement sync this week (Tue/Wed) to confirm instrument and paperwork expectations? I can bring our contracts specialist, Aditya.

Thanks — Naomi

Thanks Naomi — great walkthrough. A few answers from procurement perspective: 

- Instrument: For anything > $25k TCV we need a PO and a signed MSA; for trials under that threshold our finance team will often approve a corporate card or P-card. For clarity: the pilot is likely to be classified as trial/POC and might fit under the card rule depending on the estimated spend.
- Marketplace: AWS Marketplace is preferred by our platform team because it simplifies chargeback, but legal prefers direct contracts for any data-processing attachments (SOC2 + DPA) unless the Marketplace listing carries equivalent terms.
- Timeline: procurement is targeting an internal approval window that concludes by 2026-11-10. Legal will usually need ~3 weeks to review an MSA + SOW.

Action items for Redwood we need:
1) High-level estimate of pilot spend (monthly burn) for both hosted on-demand and a small dedicated reserved pool (so we can route to budget owners).
2) SOC 2 report (or link to your compliance page) and a redline-friendly SOW template we can share with legal.

We'd be open to a quick procurement sync on Wed 10/21 at 11am PT — will that work for you and Aditya?

-Jessica

On Mon, Oct 19, 2026 at 12:41 PM Jessica Lee <jessica@brightleaf.ai> wrote:
> Thanks Naomi — great walkthrough. A few answers from procurement perspective: ...

Thanks, Jessica — super helpful. Below are the two commercial view options and a recommended path we typically see work well given your timeline and desire to limit up-front friction.

1) Pilot (fast path) — Hosted, on-demand- What it is: Redwood hosted API, pay-as-you-go. No reserved commit; start immediately after minimal NAC and API key exchange.- Estimated monthly pilot burn: $4k–$7k (depends on query volume; estimate assumes 250k tokens/month).- Pros: fastest to launch, avoids PO for many orgs, immediate observability.- Cons: higher per-token unit cost vs reserved Dedicated.

2) Production (recommended post-pilot) — Dedicated reserved capacity (3-month starter commit)- What it is: Dedicated GPU pool with reserved throughput and a discount over hosted.- Suggested starter commitment: 3-month term at 25% discount relative to hosted list pricing; option to extend or convert consumed commit to longer term. Estimated monthly commit: $18k–$28k (for sustained 2x pilot traffic).- Pros: predictable latency and lower unit cost; isolation for sensitive workloads.- Cons: procurement will likely require a PO and MSA; slightly longer lead time to provision.

3) Private deployment — For regulated/air-gapped deployments or if your legal requires full VPC/on-prem model. This is a separate sale with onboarding and infrastructure commitments; typically >6 figures TCV and slower procurement.

Compliance & paperwork we can provide immediately:
- SOC 2 Type II report link: https://redwood.com/compliance/soc2 (or attach partial SOC2 scope if needed)- SOW template (attached): SOW-template.docx- Short commercial addendum that maps to your PO fields (we'll draft after the sync)

Attachments: 3mo-commit-dedicated-pricing.xlsx (breakdown by throughput & discount tiers), SOW-template.docx

Recommended next steps:
- If you're okay with the pilot estimate, proceed on the Hosted on-demand route so you can start before legal finishes the MSA.
- Schedule the procurement sync (Wed 10/21 11am PT works for us; Aditya will join to cover contracts and pricing).
- I'll prepare a short commercial addendum showing PO fields and a one-page statement of work for your legal to review ahead of time.

Links: HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/12345
Proposal (editable): https://app.redwood.com/proposals/RINF-2026-BL-0412

Let me know if you'd like a slightly lower starter commit or an alternate 1-month reserved option — happy to model both quickly.

Best,
